question:
We need a cloud host for a bootstrapped B2B API (single region ok, ~$400-900/mo). Priorities: predictable egress bills,
sane support for incidents, then performance. Rank these from best to worst for that brief:
AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, DigitalOcean, Linode, Vultr, Hetzner, OVHcloud, Render, Fly.io.
Research memo first, then full numbered list.

web_snippets.excerpt:
Multiple founders say AWS/GCP surprise egress bills killed margins. DigitalOcean and Linode praised for simplicity.
Vultr mentioned as "DO-like pricing, slightly more bare-metal options, support uneven but ok."
Hetzner wins on raw price in EU; several US users hesitate on latency/support hours.

Render and Fly.io love for DX; both had multi-hour platform incidents in the past year that small teams could not escalate past Discord vibe support.
Azure enterprise support is strong if you pay; useless if you do not.

Transparent bandwidth pools on many plans; object storage and optimized cloud compute in more cities than people expect.
Positions against "hyperscaler complexity" for mid-size workloads.

Hyperscalers still win if you need IAM/org policy gravity. For a single API service, hyperscaler tax is optional.
OVHcloud cheap but reputation for opaque incidents. Linode (Akamai) improved enterprise posture; less "fun" than Vultr for hobbyist root access culture.

"Hetzner if EU; Vultr/DO if US simple VMs; AWS only when customers force you."
"Fly is magical until it is not." "GCP networking is great and billing is a horror story."

scoring_note: No authoritative ranking in evidence. Activation=principal_first; chance~0.10. C0 is the null.
